notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.
Kept canonical cluster ids only; no new cluster required.
Sized for a medium-density modern kitchen with perimeter bias and one optional support cluster at most.
19.88 m2 kitchen supports a full core run and one substantial support cluster, but the room should still protect circulation and the longest usable wall.
Keep core kitchen elements longest; dishwasher is the first core item to drop if space tightens.
Storage is useful but should remain secondary to the working triangle; prefer one tall/pantry cabinet, not both, unless surplus is clearly comfortable.
Island is viable only as a compact/small footprint piece; avoid promoting it over perimeter function.
Hospitality items are nonessential in this room and should be filtered out early.
Kitchen core is wall-led and should stay off entry/circulation and center openness.
Storage is secondary and should reinforce the main wall run without blocking access.
Island/prep is optional; keep only if circulation and clearance remain intact.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Request contract is inferred from explicit brief object mentions; tier count may degrade but should not silently drop protected items.
